messages:
Priya (EngOps): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — use this thread for process Q&A about release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs. Drop short questions and we'll answer. :wave:

Ava (ENG): Quick Q — any move to 2-week releases? We're seeing hotfix churn where features land late in the cycle.

Priya (EngOps): Short answer: no org-wide switch yet. Major cadence remains monthly, but teams can opt into a 2-week slice if they get platform sign-off and add a regression checklist. We'll publish the 'release windows' doc next Tue <https://internal.redwood/release-windows>

Diego (PM): How should we map roadmap milestones to release slots? Do we treat releases as fixed slots and plan features into them, or should PMs request slots ad-hoc?

Samir (CTO): Treat release slots as capacity planning. PMs should claim a slot at sprint start. Policy: feature freeze 48h prior, canary at 10% traffic for 24h, then full rollout. If a critical perf or correctness regression appears during canary, we rollback and open a postmortem.

Lily (SRE): SLA note: hosted API target is 99.5% across last 30d for non-enterprise; Dedicated customers get contract SLAs (usually 99.9%+). For incidents: page on SEV1, follow runbook -> postmortem within 3 business days.

Ava (ENG): What counts as a 'blocking regression' for releases? Test flakiness vs deterministic failures?

Priya (EngOps): Blockers = deterministic failing integration tests, schema-breaking changes, perf regressions >20% median latency on release benchmark, or any user-facing correctness drop on golden prompts. Flakiness gets ticketed but rarely blocks unless it obscures real failures.

Samir (CTO): Adding: automated evals run on canary model — if eval score drops >5% relative to baseline on the smoke suite, we trigger rollback. We want lightweight, actionable signals (not brittle thresholds).

Ava (ENG): Nice. For oncall, are we changing rotation length or adding runbooks?

Priya (EngOps): Rotation stays weekly for now. We're adding a 'shadow day' model: shadow pairs join the pager on the Friday before their week to reduce context loss. Also updating runbooks this quarter — please ping #eng-oncall with gaps.

Diego (PM): One more — can we get a concise doc that maps release cadence -> expected lead times for feature work, e2e, and external docs? That would help PMs.

Priya (EngOps): Yes — compiling a one-pager that maps timelines (claim slot, integration window, freeze, canary, rollout). Will share by EOD Wednesday.

DeployBot: deploy 1868123690 canary started for service 'api-gateway' -> 10% traffic

Lily (SRE): saw canary, monitoring perf now :eyes:

Ava (ENG): thanks folks. This cleared up most of my questions :thumbsup:

Samir (CTO): Thanks — keep questions short here. Leadership will follow up on any unresolved items in the next all-hands. :handshake:

Priya (EngOps): Closing thread — will post the doc and link to #docs when ready. Thanks all! :tada:
